resources.name: Portacle
resources.desc: A portable and multiplatform Common Lisp environment. It ships a slightly customized Emacs with SLIME, SBCL (a popular Common Lisp implementation), Quicklisp and Git. No installation needed, so it's a very quick and easy way to get going.

resources.name: Lispbox
resources.desc: An IDE (Emacs + SLIME), Common Lisp implementation (Clozure Common Lisp) and library manager (Quicklisp), pre-packaged as archives for Windows, macOS and Linux. Descendant of "Lisp in a Box" mentioned in Practical Common Lisp.

resources.name: Lispworks Personal Edition
resources.desc: A non-Emacs based IDE for LispWorks Lisp, with some restrictions.

resources.name: Allegro Common Lisp
resources.desc: Has a free Express Edition IDE, and training videos on YouTube.

resources.name: Articulate Common Lisp
resources.desc: A HOWTO for putting together a Lisp environment, and has information on useful libraries and how to structure projects.

resources.name: The Common Lisp Hyperspec (CLHS)
resources.desc: *The* language reference document for Common Lisp. Bookmark it now.

resources.name: Chapter 7
resources.desc: Covers the Common Lisp Object System (CLOS).

resources.name: The ANSI Common Lisp Standard Draft
resources.desc: The last draft version of the ANSI INCITS 226-1994 (previously ANSI X3.226-1994) standard.

resources.name: The Common Lisp Cookbook
resources.desc: A list of useful Lisp recipes. Also contains a list of other online sources of CL information.

resources.name: Common Lisp the Language (2nd Edition) by Guy L. Steele
resources.desc: A description of the Common Lisp language from just before it was standardized by ANSI. Don't use it as a reference.

resources.name: Cliki on CLtL2
resources.desc: Claims it has more useful descriptions of LOOP and FORMAT than the CLHS does.

resources.name: Stack Overflow on CLtL2
resources.desc: Some recommend using CLtL2 for insight and inspiration, but to use the CLHS when programming.

resources.name: A list of differences between CLtL2 and the ANSI Common Lisp specification.
Chapter 28
resources.desc: Covers the Common Lisp Object System.

resources.name: Common Lisp: A Gentle Introduction to Symbolic Computation by David S. Touretzky
resources.desc: a good introduction for people new to programming. Contains code for really useful utilities like DTRACE and SDRAW.

resources.name: Common Lisp: An interactive approach by Stuart C. Shapiro
resources.desc: A textbook that teaches mainly through the use of exercises.

resources.name: Practical Common Lisp by Peter Seibel
resources.desc: A great introduction for experienced programmers, and tries to highlight from the very beginning what makes CL different to other languages.

resources.name: Common Lisp Koans
resources.desc: Not exactly a book, but a set of koans to help you learn the language.

resources.name: On Lisp by Paul Graham
resources.desc: A great book for intermediately experienced Lispers.

resources.name: Let Over Lambda by Doug Hoyte
resources.desc: An advanced book on Lisp Macros.

resources.name: Comments on Let Over Lambda
resources.desc: Several people recommend that you be comfortable with On Lisp before reading this book, and that the start is slow.

resources.name: The chapter on closures
resources.desc: Has several non-trivial examples, and demonstrates the power of this feature.

resources.name: Paradigms of Artificial Intelligence Programming by Peter Norvig
resources.desc: Has many interesting applications of Lisp, but is no longer a good reference for AI.

resources.name: Land of Lisp by Conrad Barski, MD
resources.desc: A fun introduction to Lisp that uses comics and has you writing games.

resources.name: ANSI Common Lisp by Paul Graham
resources.desc: Good as a reference, covers CLOS, and has several example program implementations.

resources.name: Common Lisp Recipes by Edmund Weitz
resources.desc: A great set of Common Lisp patterns.

resources.name: Object-Oriented Programming in Common Lisp by Sonya E. Keene
resources.desc: An in-depth description of the CLOS, and shows how to use it with example applications.

resources.name: The Art of the Metaobject Protocol by Gregor Kiczales, Jim des Rivieres, and Daniel G. Bobrow
resources.desc: Describes the CLOS Metaobject Protocol (MOP).

resources.name: Chapters 5 and 6 (available online)
resources.desc: The specification of a metaobject protocol extension to CLOS, by Robert Strandh.

resources.name: Adam Tornhill on AMOP
resources.desc: Recommends reading Practical Common Lisp, then Object-Oriented Programming in Common Lisp, and then AMOP.

resources.name: Lisp Subreddit
resources.desc: An active community, and has loads of useful links and reference documents in the sidebar.

resources.name: Common Lisp Subreddit
resources.desc: The Subreddit for Common Lisp.

resources.name: Exercism's Common Lisp track
resources.desc: An excellent way to learn the language through practice, have your code reviewed, and to discuss solutions with other people.

resources.name: Lisp Discord server
resources.desc: Is a Discord for Lisp. Has a channel dedicated to Common Lisp and will happily answer questions.

resources.name: Quicklisp
resources.desc: A package management platform for Lisp libraries.

resources.name: Quickdocs
resources.desc: Documentation for projects in Quicklisp.

resources.name: State of the Common Lisp Ecosystem, 2015
resources.desc: Article about what libraries you should use, and why.

resources.name: Articulate Common Lisp
resources.desc: Lists some useful libraries.

resources.name: Allegro Common Lisp (ACL)
resources.desc: Commercial, but has a free Express Edition.

resources.name: CMUCL manual and other useful information
LispWorks
resources.desc: Commercial, but as mentioned previously, has a Personal Edition with minor limitations.

resources.name: Steel Bank Common Lisp (SBCL)
resources.desc: My personal favorite.

resources.name: Scieneer Common Lisp (SCL)
resources.desc: A commercial Linux and Unix implementation, but has an unrestricted free evaluation and non-commercial use version.
